statement: If two numbers be prime to one another, the second will not be to any other number as the first is to the second.
heath_proof: For let the two numbers A, B be prime to one another; I say that B is not to any other number as A is to B. For, if possible, as A is to B, so let B be to C. Now A, B are prime, primes are also least, [VII. 21] and the least numbers measure those which have the same ratio the same number of times, the antecedent the antecedent and the consequent the consequent; [VII. 20] therefore A measures B as antecedent antecedent. But it also measures itself; therefore A measures A, B which are prime to one another: which is absurd. Therefore B will not be to C, as A is to B.
ai_proof_text:
9.16
**Statement:** If two numbers be prime to one another, the second will not be to any other number as the first is to the second.

**Step 1.** Let A, B be two numbers prime to one another. I say that B is not to any other number as A is to B.

**Step 2.** For, if possible, let there be some number C such that, as A is to B, so is B to C.

**Step 3.** Since A, B are prime to one another, they are the least of those numbers which have the same ratio with them [7.21].

**Step 4.** Now the least numbers of those which have the same ratio with them measure those which have the same ratio the same number of times, the greater the greater and the less the less, that is, the antecedent the antecedent and the consequent the consequent [7.20]. Since A, B are the least numbers in the ratio of A to B, and B, C have that same ratio (Step 2), it follows that A measures B and B measures C, the same number of times.

**Step 5.** But A also measures itself. Therefore A measures both A and B, so that A is a common measure of A and B.

**Step 6.** Now A is a number, that is, a multitude composed of units, and hence is not a unit [D7.2]. Thus A, B are measured as a common measure by a number other than the unit. But A, B are prime to one another, that is, they are measured by an unit alone as a common measure [D7.12]. This is absurd.

**Step 7.** Therefore there is no number C such that, as A is to B, so is B to C. Hence, if two numbers be prime to one another, the second will not be to any other number as the first is to the second. Q.E.D.
